youtube_title: Wanatah, Indiana: the Palm Sunday tornado of 1965 (Wanatah request)
youtube:
You asked for Wanatah! On Palm Sunday, April 11, 1965, an unusually warm spring day, a tornado touched down in Porter County and crossed into LaPorte County. Near Wanatah it tore apart homes, then destroyed more homes and barns near Kingsford Heights. Warnings went out, but many people never got them, and the Weather Service says its South Bend office had no radar; it relied on phone calls with radar operators in Chicago. This tornado killed no one, but tornadoes killed more than 130 people across Indiana that day. Afterward, the Weather Bureau's "tornado forecast" got a new name: today we call it a tornado watch. Comment your town, and it could be next! #Wanatah #LaPorteCounty #Indiana #PalmSunday #Tornado #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn; the farm, the church and the people are generic, and no one is shown hurt. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: National Weather Service, Northern Indiana, Chicago and Indianapolis offices (Palm Sunday 1965 pages); Storm Prediction Center history; Thomas P. Grazulis, Significant Tornadoes; The Times of Northwest Indiana (2015); WTHR (2005); Janis Thornton, The 1965 Palm Sunday Tornadoes in Indiana; Towne Post; LiveScience; WDET; The Weather Network; FOX6 Milwaukee; NOAA NWS Heritage; ustornadoes.com. The sources disagree on where exactly it touched down, the exact time, the path length and the rating, and on Indiana's death toll (137 to 145), so this gives none of those. More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history

factcheck: Independent check Nov. 15, 2026, not ready on first pass (5 fixes), fixed before scheduling: touchdown spot conflict (official track from south of Crown Point vs south of Valparaiso) so 'Porter County'; 'Warnings went out, but many people never got them' (South Bend had warned LaPorte County shortly before); 'homes' instead of 'homes and farms', 'more homes and barns near Kingsford Heights'; trees bare for early April; no full moon; palms off the churchgoers; Facebook 'Later that day' instead of 'That evening'. The checker was given the story file with the writer's source notes (the playbook says to give it only the script, text and pictures); it researched independently (NWS Indianapolis, SPC history, Grazulis, Britannica) all the same.
